answer.answer: Current authentication mode: OAuth 2.1. Beginning in 2026, Elm API requires OAuth 2.1 and no longer accepts API keys (elm-auth-2026). Previously valid: in 2025, Elm API required API keys (elm-auth-2025); that requirement is now historical and superseded. Both snapshots carry the same subject_id (elm-api) and lineage_id (elm-auth), so this is a temporal change to one subject, not a change of subject. Note that 'current' is bounded by the latest supplied snapshot (2026); no later evidence is provided to confirm the requirement beyond that date.
change_events: Beginning in 2026, Elm API changed its required authentication mode from API keys to OAuth 2.1 (elm-auth-2026; prior state documented for 2025 in elm-auth-2025).
Beginning in 2026, Elm API no longer accepts API keys, ending the API-key requirement that was in effect in 2025 (elm-auth-2026; elm-auth-2025).
current_truths: As of the latest supplied snapshot (2026), Elm API requires OAuth 2.1 (elm-auth-2026).
As of the latest supplied snapshot (2026), Elm API no longer accepts API keys (elm-auth-2026).
historical_truths: In 2025, Elm API required API keys (elm-auth-2025). This was valid for 2025 and is now superseded by the 2026 change to OAuth 2.1 (elm-auth-2026).
unresolved: No snapshot dated after 2026 is supplied, so whether OAuth 2.1 remains the required mode beyond 2026 cannot be confirmed from the supplied sources (elm-auth-2026).
The snapshots do not specify the exact effective date within 2026, any transition or grace period, or how existing API keys were handled at deprecation (elm-auth-2025, elm-auth-2026).
OAuth 2.1 implementation details (flows, scopes, token lifetimes, endpoints) are not specified in the supplied snapshots (elm-auth-2026).
